newsitem.title: CHINA: China suspends copper imports, halts sales - Trade.
newsitem.headline: China suspends copper imports, halts sales - Trade.

text.p: China has suspended copper imports and domestic copper traders have been ordered not to sell their copper in order to support the price of the red metal, Chinese metal trading sources said on Monday.

The directive was issued after a two-day non-ferrous metals seminar in Beijing last week between government officials and delegates from the Chinese base metals industry, traders and analysts in Shanghai said.
Government officials in the capital could not immediately be reached for comment.
A Chinese copper market analyst said the directive also instructed long-position holders on the Shanghai Metal Exchange (SME) not to sell "in order to prevent any price falls".
The trading sources said the SME had also been ordered not to allow copper prices on the exchange to go above 24,500 yuan ($2,952) a tonne.
"This is seen as a suitable price for long-position holders," a local trader.
SME president Hu Yuezheng told Reuters on Friday he knew nothing of the directive.

Shanghai copper futures opened up on Monday on talk of the the state directive. The most active June 1996 contract opened at 23,800 yuan ($2,867) a tonne, up 130. It rose further to 24,080 early in the trading.

Local dealers said the directive was aimed at supporting loss-making state copper mines, but added that they believed it would be impossible to hold the domestic market within set price limits for long if there were opposing trends in the world market.
The London Metal Exchange three-month copper price was slightly firmer at $2,360/$2,365 a tonne at 0330 GMT on Monday compared with its close at $2,356 on Friday.
